title: Interest rates (Bank Rate and gilt yields)
headline: Markets now price gilts above the OBR's 4.5%. A point costs about £15bn.
description: How much higher or lower interest rates are than the OBR assumed in March 2026, sustained across the forecast. Higher rates raise the cost of servicing government debt.

baselinePolicy.text: OBR conditioning assumption, March 2026: Bank Rate averages 3.6% over 2026 to 2030; 10-year gilt yield 4.5%; 30-year gilt yield 5.3% (market prices in the 10 working days to 22 January 2026).

control.formatLabel: percentage points versus the OBR assumption

considerations.text: Gilt yields rose sharply after the March 2026 forecast. In September 2026 the 10-year yield was roughly 0.5 to 0.7 percentage points above the OBR's assumption and 30-year yields were the highest since 1998. Analysts estimated this alone removed about £10bn of headroom.

Higher rates also raise the interest cost of any extra borrowing you choose (shown as the mechanical debt-interest line). A full OBR forecast would also change growth and inflation in response; this tool does not.
